purpose: Business-level smoke tests for each kiln version upgrade. Run after build, before publishing or tagging a release.

journeys.title: CLI contract stays stable
journeys.businessValue: Developers can discover and invoke kiln the same way after an upgrade.

cases.name: help lists init, add, inspect, doctor
version prints package version
unknown command exits non-zero
add without capability exits non-zero
add unsupported capability exits non-zero
inspect outside a project exits non-zero
init rejects missing, invalid, and existing targets

journeys.title: Onboard a new Next.js app
journeys.businessValue: A developer can scaffold, add env + auth, and ship a working Next.js app.

cases.name: init scaffolds Next.js app router files
dry-run add env does not write files
add env creates DATABASE_URL in .env.example
add env --var merges custom keys
add auth preserves package.json and env vars
ownership.json tracks env and auth resources
inspect reports Next.js app router project
doctor passes on generated project
re-running add env is a no-op
generated app production-builds

journeys.title: Existing kiln projects keep working
journeys.businessValue: Teams already using kiln can upgrade the CLI without rewriting their apps.

cases.name: example app inspect still detects Next.js and ownership
example app doctor does not fail
example app still production-builds
re-applying auth on example is idempotent
